The requester asks for a distinct randomly chosen complex test concept that can show newly integrated spring fashion meaning in an image using the attached portrait. The title of the conversation supplies spring fashion as the topic. The ferry-landing scene, notice sheet, fastening gesture, clothing colors and precise constructions are independent authorial choices, not user locks. An ordinary repair at the moment a boat returns gives the structure-rich photograph a present purpose. The resolved saved controls are sensual 1, fetish 0, creativity 1, surreal 0, emphasis sensual-led; subtle human warmth supports the scene, while practical geometry and restrained visual echoes provide complexity without an added surreal treatment.

A spring fashion photograph of a person guided by the supplied reference, with visible facial features and short black hair guided by the supplied portrait. Spring clothing structures are visibly worn within a particular moment of ordinary work. At a small ferry landing just after morning rain, she sits on a low timber bench and clips the loosened upper corner of a rain-warped route sheet back onto the wire of a narrow notice frame beside her. The other upper corner is already fastened; a damp crease runs diagonally across the paper, and a small ferry is entering the gap between the landing posts. Her fingertips finish the fastening as her chin turns slightly toward the returning boat, a small easing of her lips giving the otherwise concentrated face an approachable warmth. Her pale apricot blouse has a soft diagonal drape descending from the left shoulder toward the opposite waist. A fabric flower is fixed at the left shoulder: separate curled petal edges gather around a compact center, and the flower's base sits flush against the blouse at that single attachment point. The folds radiate from beneath that base instead of floating beside it. Her sage skirt has an upper wrap panel crossing the waist, its diagonal free edge visibly lying over the under-panel; below that edge, a broad lower section falls in repeated narrow vertical pleats. The pleats open slightly over the nearer bent knee and continue into long folds below it. These are distinct constructions with readable edges, attachment and overlap rather than a mass of rippling fabric. Her hips are supported by the bench, her torso faces the camera in a relaxed three-quarter orientation, and her left palm rests beside her hip on the seat. Her right arm reaches sideways to the notice frame at shoulder level, with the elbow softly bent and the right thumb and forefinger pressing a wooden clip over the paper and wire. The frame stands close enough that her shoulder remains over her seated pelvis. Both feet rest flat on the planks, the nearer foot half a shoe-length ahead and angled outward. The skirt ends above her ankles. Each ivory ballet flat has a rounded shallow toe and thin ribbons threaded from the shoe's side attachments across the instep in clear X crossings, then continuing around the ankle into a small tied bow; the ribbon paths remain visible against the skin and separate from the skirt hem. Use a vertical head-to-toe view from just below her seated eye level, looking obliquely across the bench so the face, shoulder flower, wrap edge, lower pleats and both shoes all have room to resolve. The board occupies a slim zone beside her reaching hand, leaving the center of the clothing visible. Darkened wet planks and a pale reflection under the bench carry the recent rain; the small boat and bright channel sit farther behind her. Soft directional daylight gives the flower a shallow contact shadow, catches the outer edges of the skirt pleats and keeps the ribbon crossings distinct. Let her quiet concentration lead, the repaired corner connect the scene to a returning journey, and the repeated folding rhythms of paper and clothing support that moment. The photograph feels naturally inhabited, with crisp tactile detail on the subject and a gently quieter background.

definitions.principle: These creative definitions guide agent-owned choices within requester meaning, not clinical classifications. Zero/off disables added treatment, never removes explicitly requested content or artistic judgment. Expression levels describe prominence in the whole image; creativity levels describe interpretive freedom. Neither measures exposure percentages, detail quotas, quality scores, or native image-model parameters. Intensity and expression are separate choices; higher intensity does not prescribe a garment, material or expression category. Creativity leaves style, extra props and surreal treatment open to the request and artistic judgment. Emphasis directs only active sensual and fetish axes without changing their intensities. Popular permits familiar appeal without requiring trend search; overt is an available expression, not the mandatory meaning of level three. Choose a coherent expression suited to this particular scene. Sensual and fetish may share the same expressive choice.

sensual.definition: Broadly interpreted human attraction and desire, including everyday, popular, intimate, suggestive, seductive, and overt expressions.

levels.0: No added sensual treatment; preserve explicitly requested content.
levels.1: This expression is a subtle supporting quality.
levels.2: This expression is clearly readable in the image.
levels.3: This expression leads the image's appeal and direction.

fetish.definition: Sexual attraction or arousal focused on particular objects, bodily features, clothing, materials, roles, situations, behaviors, or sensory qualities that carry special erotic significance, interpreted broadly beyond conventional fetish aesthetics.

levels.0: No added fetish treatment; preserve explicitly requested content.
levels.1: This focus is a subtle supporting quality.
levels.2: This focus is clearly readable in the image.
levels.3: This focus leads the image's appeal and direction.

adult_appeal_emphasis.definition: Relative leadership of the active sensual and fetish axes within one coherent expression.

choice_descriptions.auto: Let the higher effective intensity lead; equal active intensities share leadership. Add no emphasis when both axes are inactive.
choice_descriptions.sensual_led: Let broad attraction and desire lead, with any active distinctive fascination supporting the expression.
choice_descriptions.balanced: Give both active axes comparable influence within one coherent expression; separate styling details are not required.
choice_descriptions.fetish_led: Let the distinctive focus of attraction or fascination lead, with any active sensual expression supporting it.

creativity.definition: Freedom to interpret unspecified choices and explore relationships within the request.

levels.0: Realize the request directly, filling only what is needed for a coherent image.
levels.1: Introduce restrained variations close to the requested direction.
levels.2: Actively reinterpret open choices into a coherent authorial direction.
levels.3: Boldly explore unexpected relationships and interpretations while preserving the request's core meaning.

viewer_experience.definition: Expose the detailed viewer-experience review when enabled. Always consider the intended impression in interpreted_intent, even when this additional review is off.

reference_edit_mode.definition: Use the selected reference-edit workflow only within the requester's reference-use scope. Record that scope in the core; a face/hair reference does not lock clothing, body shape or composition and does not prove identity. Off does not discard a supplied reference.

surreal.definition: Added departures from ordinary reality, interpreted broadly across space, scale, causality, materials, and atmosphere, including dreamlike, uncanny, symbolic, and impossible relationships.

levels.1: Surreal qualities are a subtle supporting presence.
levels.2: Surreal qualities are clearly readable in the image.
levels.3: Surreal qualities lead the image's main impression and direction; a single coherent relationship may carry this prominence.

trend_layer.definition: Consider the chosen treatment from the initial composition. Refine it later without adding it twice. Off does not remove a treatment explicitly present in the request.

Spring clothing structures are visibly worn within a particular moment of ordinary work. At a small ferry landing just after morning rain, she sits on a low timber bench and clips the loosened upper corner of a rain-warped route sheet back onto the wire of a narrow notice frame beside her. The other upper corner is already fastened; a damp crease runs diagonally across the paper, and a small ferry is entering the gap between the landing posts. Her fingertips finish the fastening as her chin turns slightly toward the returning boat, a small easing of her lips giving the otherwise concentrated face an approachable warmth. Her pale apricot blouse has a soft diagonal drape descending from the left shoulder toward the opposite waist. A fabric flower is fixed at the left shoulder: separate curled petal edges gather around a compact center, and the flower's base sits flush against the blouse at that single attachment point. The folds radiate from beneath that base instead of floating beside it. Her sage skirt has an upper wrap panel crossing the waist, its diagonal free edge visibly lying over the under-panel; below that edge, a broad lower section falls in repeated narrow vertical pleats. The pleats open slightly over the nearer bent knee and continue into long folds below it. These are distinct constructions with readable edges, attachment and overlap rather than a mass of rippling fabric. Her hips are supported by the bench, her torso faces the camera in a relaxed three-quarter orientation, and her left palm rests beside her hip on the seat. Her right arm reaches sideways to the notice frame at shoulder level, with the elbow softly bent and the right thumb and forefinger pressing a wooden clip over the paper and wire. The frame stands close enough that her shoulder remains over her seated pelvis. Both feet rest flat on the planks, the nearer foot half a shoe-length ahead and angled outward. The skirt ends above her ankles. Each ivory ballet flat has a rounded shallow toe and thin ribbons threaded from the shoe's side attachments across the instep in clear X crossings, then continuing around the ankle into a small tied bow; the ribbon paths remain visible against the skin and separate from the skirt hem. Use a vertical head-to-toe view from just below her seated eye level, looking obliquely across the bench so the face, shoulder flower, wrap edge, lower pleats and both shoes all have room to resolve. The board occupies a slim zone beside her reaching hand, leaving the center of the clothing visible. Darkened wet planks and a pale reflection under the bench carry the recent rain; the small boat and bright channel sit farther behind her. Soft directional daylight gives the flower a shallow contact shadow, catches the outer edges of the skirt pleats and keeps the ribbon crossings distinct. Let her quiet concentration lead, the repaired corner connect the scene to a returning journey, and the repeated folding rhythms of paper and clothing support that moment. The photograph feels naturally inhabited, with crisp tactile detail on the subject and a gently quieter background.
